November 29 1922

REPORT ON Russians apply for passports to Australia

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

Nikolas Idanoff is a native of Bugilma, Samora Province, European Russia. He is 26 years old and is unmarried. He was a medical student until the outbreak of the revolution in Russia when he joined the Czecho-Slovak Army and served with them as a hospital attendant. He afterwards served with Kolchak and other anti-Bolshevik detachments in Siberia until the occupation of Vladivostock by the "Reds". He came to Shanghai from Vladivostock on October 25, 1922 and since his arrival has lived at 332 Broadway. His passage to Australia is being paid by Dr. Panek, a Czecho-Slovak under whom Idanoff served in Siberia. His reason for choosing Brisbane is because the fare is cheaper than to Sydney or Melbourne and also because he believes that for a man with his limitations as regards language, etc. employment will be easier to obtain in Queensland than in New South Wales or Victoria. He intends at first to endeavour to obtain some kind of work on a farm of which he had had experience but eventually to continue his studies in the medical profession.

Ivan Bessaroboff is a native of Shatoi, Tarek District, South Eastern Russia. He is 26 years old and is unmarried. He is a motor mechanic by trade. He served in the Russian Army on the Persian front during the great war. After being demobilised in 1918 he returned to his home and afterwards joined in an anti-Bolshevik revolt and was forced to retreat into Mesopotamia from where he was repatriated to

关于俄国人申请前往澳大利亚护照的报告

由 D. I. Sullivan 呈报 经由 [签名] 转呈

先生，

Nikolas Idanoff 系欧洲俄罗斯萨马拉省（Samora Province）布吉尔马（Bugilma）人。现年26岁，未婚。在俄国革命爆发前，他是一名医科学生；革命爆发后，他加入捷克斯洛伐克军队，担任医院勤务员。此后，他在西伯利亚随高尔察克（Kolchak）及其他反布尔什维克分队服役，直至“红军”占领符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）。他于1922年10月25日从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海，抵沪后一直居住在百老汇路332号。他前往澳大利亚的旅费由 Panek 博士支付，Panek 博士是捷克斯洛伐克人，Idanoff 曾在西伯利亚在其麾下服役。他选择布里斯班的原因是，该地船票比前往悉尼或墨尔本便宜，而且他认为，鉴于他在语言等方面的局限，在昆士兰州比在新南威尔士州或维多利亚州更容易找到工作。他打算起初设法在农场找份工作，因为他有过相关经验，但最终希望继续从事医学专业的学习。

Ivan Bessaroboff 系俄罗斯东南部塔雷克区（Tarek District）沙托伊（Shatoi）人。现年26岁，未婚。职业为汽车机械师。大战期间，他曾在波斯战线的俄国军队中服役。1918年复员后，他返回家乡，随后参加了一次反布尔什维克起义，并被迫撤退至美索不达米亚，从那里他被英国当局遣返至

Vladivostock via Bombay by the British Authorities in August
1921. In September 1921 he joined the Siberian flotilla
under the Vladivostock Government where he stayed until
March 31, 1922 when he was invalided out of the service.
He came to Shanghai by the S.S. "Shinlee" in April 1922
and lived at 805 Broadway for about three months. He then
obtained a job as fireman on a Dutch vessel called the S.S.
"Zosma" and did one voyage calling at ports on the Chinese,
Japanese, and Russian coasts. The voyage lasted five
weeks and on returning to Shanghai he lived at 679 Broadway
for about two months when he removed to 332 Broadway where
he has since resided. He has no money and is looking for
an opportunity to work his passage to Australia. He is not
particular as what part of Australia he goes to and has no
particular wish to go to Brisbane except that his friend
Jdanoff is going there. Both Jdanoff and Bessaroboff are
almost destitute and are trying to get away from Shanghai
as quickly as possible. There is nothing against either
of the applicants in Police records.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,

D. I.

D. C. I.

1921年8月经孟买由英国当局遣返至符拉迪沃斯托克。1921年9月，他加入符拉迪沃斯托克政府辖下的西伯利亚舰队，一直服役至1922年3月31日因病退役。他于1922年4月乘“新利”轮（S.S. "Shinlee"）抵达上海，在百老汇路805号居住了约三个月。随后，他在一艘名为“佐斯玛”号（S.S. "Zosma"）的荷兰船只上找到一份司炉工的工作，并完成了一次航行，停靠中国、日本和俄罗斯沿海港口。航程持续了五周，返回上海后，他在百老汇路679号居住了约两个月，随后搬至百老汇路332号，此后一直居住于此。他身无分文，正在寻找机会以做工抵偿前往澳大利亚的船费。他对前往澳大利亚的具体地点并不挑剔，除了因为他的朋友 Jdanoff 要去那里外，他并没有特别想去布里斯班的愿望。Jdanoff 和 Bessaroboff 两人都几乎一贫如洗，正试图尽快离开上海。警察档案中没有任何针对这两名申请人的不良记录。

此致，
您顺从的仆人，

D. I.

副督察长

-Slovak under whom Idanoff served in Siberia, and his
reason for choosing Brisbane is because the fare is
cheaper than to Sydney or Melbourne and also because
he believes that for a man with his limitations as
regards language, etc., employment will be easier to
obtain in Queensland than in New South Wales or Victoria.
He intends at first to endeavour to obtain some kind of
work on a farm, of which he has had experience, but
eventually to continue his studies in the medical
profession.

Confidential
British Consulate-General.
Shanghai.
4859
29/11/22

No. 234
Dated, the 24th November, 1922

My dear Hilton - Johnson.

A Russian named Nikolas Idanoff is applying at
the Consulate for a passport or visa to Australia and has
beenfathered in some mysterious way by J.S.Little. Every-
thing about the man seems suspicious and apparently no one
knows who he really is. The fact that he is going to -
Brisbane - a centre of Bolshevism in Australia - also -
strikes me as suspicious particularly in view of the fact
that he says he does not know anybody in Australia. I
believe Idanoff lives with another Russian who is also try-
ing to go to Australia called Serserakoff at 332 West -
Broadway.

I should be grateful if you would let me know as
soon as possible anything that can be ascertained regarding
these two men.

Yours sincerely,
（签名）

Major J. R. Hilton-Johnson,

Dcl
I. O.

1922年11月29日

第234号
日期：1922年11月24日

亲爱的 Hilton - Johnson：

一名名叫 Nikolas Idanoff 的俄国人正在领事馆申请前往澳大利亚的护照或签证，并以某种神秘的方式得到了 J.S.Little 的庇护。此人的各方面情况似乎都令人可疑，显然没人知道他的真实身份。事实上，他要去的是——布里斯班——澳大利亚的布尔什维主义中心——这一事实也令我感到可疑，特别是考虑到他说他在澳大利亚不认识任何人。我相信 Idanoff 与另一名同样试图前往澳大利亚、名叫 Serserakoff 的俄国人同住于西百老汇路332号。

如能尽快告知有关这两人的任何可查证信息，我将不胜感激。

此致，
（签名）

J. R. Hilton-Johnson 少校，

Dcl
情报官
